newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals slip as rupiah topples.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals slip as rupiah topples.

text.p: Southeast Asian currencies carried on sliding on Tuesday as the Indonesian rupiah dropped through a key level and the hitherto sanguine Hong Kong dollar edged into the spotlight.

The rupiah fell back through the 3,000 to the dollar level on selling by Jakarta players in thin lunch time markets and at 0425 GMT was quoted at 3,010/20 against an opening of 2,960/80. The rupiah briefly touched a low of 3,005 on Monday afternoon.
"So far all we saw were Jakarta names out there," a Singapore dealer said. There was no sign of central bank intervention, he said.
Dealers said the rupiah had strengthened earlier as U.S. funds booked profits in dollar/rupiah around the 2,990 level and bought the dollar/baht.

"The funds believe there are signs Thailand's two-tier market may be lifted and then the onshore market would want to grab dollars from the offshore," said the head of Asian currencies at a European bank in Singapore.
He said the cross play in the rupiah/baht had pushed dollar/baht to a high of 32.75 in offshore markets.

"The funds probably see more signs of problems in Thailand. The baht behaved quite well after the attack on the rupiah last week, but its current weakness is mainly due to political uncertainty in Thailand," he said.
Dealers said the market was nervous about an internal conflict in Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's New Aspiration Party after last week's cabinet reshuffle.
The baht was quoted at 32.44/54 to the dollar onshore against 32.05/32.15 late on Monday. It was at 32.65/32.75 offshore against 32.20/32.40.

The rupiah fall tipped the Malaysian ringgit over the 2.80 to the dollar level. It was quoted at 2.7970/8020 at 0425 GMT after being sandwiched between dollar bids at 2.79 and offers from Malaysian exporters at 2.80.
The Singapore dollar also suffered some spillover weakness from the rupiah, but activity was subdued, dealers said.
They said the Hong Kong dollar, Asia's strongest currency peg, was attracting growing attention from speculators.
"Once all these regional currencies find a suitable level, the speculators will target the Hong Kong dollar," the European bank dealer in Singapore said.
"Hong Kong's economy is still sound and the stock market is stronger than most in the region. But the market is looking at relative competitiveness and Hong Kong is a big exporter," he said.
The continuing weakness of the region's currencies could increase pressure on Hong Kong to abandon its U.S. dollar peg, the dealer added.

But Hong Kong was adamant the peg would be protected and speculators who attacked it would be "burned" with high interest rates that would make it too expensive to launch a major operation against the currency.
Government chief Tung Chee-hwa said on Monday any speculative attack on the Hong Kong dollar was "bound to fail".

Hong Kong interbank rates shot up on Monday on fears of a speculative attack. Dealers said the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) might tighten liquidity to make it expensive for speculators to fund their positions.
The Taiwan dollar was weak, but the central bank's continued defence of the T$28.727 level limited its decline.
The Taiwan dollar was quoted at T$28.726/727 at 0425 GMT against Saturday's T$28.720 close. A range of T$28.710-727 was expected for the day.
